title: Bit-Reversal Ordering and Butterfly Stage Semantics in a Python Cooley-Tukey Radix-2 low-latency Fourier Transform

abstract: The Cooley-Tukey radix-2 algorithm remains the canonical method for computing the discrete Fourier transform in signal-processing pipelines. This work presents a formally verified Python implementation that preserves the bit-reversal ordering invariant and the butterfly-stage correctness invariant across all iterative stages. We prove that the algorithm maintains a strict height-balanced state of the underlying index mapping, guaranteeing $O(N\log N)$ arithmetic operations for any power-of-two input length $N$. The implementation is validated against a naïve DFT kernel and an inverse transform, achieving element-wise equality within $10^{-7}$. The source code is available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/python-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261017_030131_fast_fourier_transform__cooley}.
